subject.title: Embedded runner: freshly streamed thinking signatures intermittently invalid on replay (Anthropic); recovery wrapper never fires because error text is genericized

question: Should OpenClaw resolve the remaining Anthropic signed-thinking replay problem by landing the narrower completed-turn replay policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383, or keep preserving all Claude 4 thinking blocks and rely on recovery?
rationale: Current source and Anthropic docs create a real compatibility tradeoff between omitting prior-turn thinking to prevent session bricks and preserving signed thinking for provider-native replay/prompt-cache behavior.

options.title: Land the narrow replay-policy fix
options.body: Scope replay to current/active tool-turn thinking for non-Fable Claude models, with focused live/provider proof and upgrade notes before merge.

options.title: Keep preserve-all replay
options.body: Continue replaying all signed thinking blocks and rely on recovery, accepting that prevention remains incomplete when recovery does not fire or is absent from shipped releases.

options.title: Defer to broader session migration
options.body: Treat this as dependent on the larger session/transcript migration, leaving production users on recovery and manual transcript repair longer.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow replay-policy fix
recommendation.body: Scope replay to current/active tool-turn thinking for non-Fable Claude models, with focused live/provider proof and upgrade notes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He already split the recovery half from the still-open prevention half in this thread and has recent provenance in the relevant recovery/replay code path.
